original.target_description: Unresolved correspondence: supplied description concerns valuing; Gonnerman’s first survey (section 3.1, p. 198 / PDF p. 7) tests desires in racist versus liberal George vignettes. Section 3.2 (pp. 198–199 / PDF pp. 7–8) tests moral beliefs. Neither is a primary test of valuing.

es.location: p. 198, section 3.1 (PDF p. 7); p. 199, section 3.2 (PDF p. 8)
es.quote: Whereas Knobe and Roedder asked about Georges’ states of valuing, we asked ... about their desires. ... A t-test revealed that the difference between these means scores is ... statistically significant (p < 0.05).

notes: Only es_value_o is assigned. All other fields/sides are unassigned placeholders. Target was not selected by row order or numerical matching. The supplied study identifier 1 points toward the first survey, but the supplied valuing outcome conflicts with the expressly stated desires outcome. First-survey printed candidates are condition means 0.320 and −1.05, with a t-test reported only as p < 0.05; no numeric t statistic or named standardized effect size is printed. The second survey reports moral-belief condition means 1.192 and −0.286 and a t-test only as p < 0.05, again without numeric t or named standardized effect size. These are candidate descriptions, not extracted target statistics. No effect conversion was performed. The valuing results discussed in section 2 are attributed to Knobe and Roedder (2006), not primary Gonnerman data. Target PDF pages 7 and 8 were rendered and inspected. No analytic N was assigned or calculated.
